result.title: Lightweight Frame Compensation for Real-Time Polyp Segmentation under Frame Skipping
result.summary: Real-time polyp segmentation in computer-assisted colonoscopy is hampered by the difficulty of deploying high-accuracy models under strict latency budgets. Frame skipping, which performs inference every K frames and reuses or interpolates the rest, improves throughput but introduces motion blur and lesion misalignment that degrade temporal consistency. To close this gap, we propose the Lightweight Frame Compensator (LFC), a 77K-parameter plug-and-play module inserted before a frozen segmentation backbone. Operating on a three-frame window, LFC fuses consecutive frames via spatio-temporal attention into a single compensated frame, and is trained only on pseudo-labels generated by a differently seeded model, without any expert annotation. Experiments on three polyp video benchmarks show that LFC recovers most of the accuracy degraded by direct frame skipping and, in several settings, reaches the accuracy of frame-by-frame inference, while retaining a 2.05X--2.55X throughput gain. We further evaluate the temporal stability of three backbones spanning CNN, pyramid Transformer, and global-attention Transformer architectures, revealing a spectrum of sensitivity to frame skipping that arises from how locally or globally each architecture aggregates misaligned input. The compensation gain of LFC follows this spectrum: it is largest for high-capacity Transformer backbones, which achieve the best static accuracy but suffer the most under skip-frame inference. LFC thus offers a lightweight, pluggable, and deployment-friendly route to real-time polyp segmentation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 77K 参数的即插即用轻量帧补偿模块 LFC，在三帧窗口内以时空注意力把跳帧输入融合为单帧补偿帧，放在冻结的分割骨干之前，仅用伪标签训练；在三个息肉视频基准上恢复跳帧导致的精度损失并保持约 2 倍以上吞吐，同时比较 CNN 与 Transformer 骨干对跳帧的敏感度差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 跳帧条件下的低开销视觉证据重建与冻结骨干前的状态刷新，可能为 LVR 中减少视觉采样后的信息补全与 latent 状态更新提供线索；其架构敏感度谱系可供核查「省计算」与「证据保真」之间的权衡。
